facility_roles.quote: In 2013, Brookhaven's magnetic storage ring was transported from Long Island, New York, to Fermilab in Batavia, Illinois.

intervals.label: experiment proposed
intervals.note: Start is the 'date_proposed' field of the INSPIRE experiment record. The interval ends in January 2010, where the next interval (approval, from the record's 'date_approved' field) begins.

intervals.label: experiment approved
intervals.note: 'date_approved' field of the INSPIRE experiment record. End date capped at the start of the ring-relocation/construction interval below so it does not bleed into the later, separately-documented 2014-08..2017-04 gap (during which the ring was known to be under physical reassembly, not merely 'approved').

intervals.label: storage ring relocated from BNL and reassembled at Fermilab (MC-1)
intervals.locator: CERN Courier, 27 October 2014 (Hertzog and Roberts), second paragraph
intervals.note: The ring left Brookhaven and arrived at Fermilab in summer 2013 (CERN Courier, 27 October 2014); re-assembly of the storage ring began in the new MC-1 building during summer 2014 (same article). The end is therefore given at year precision, 2014; the article gives no month, and reassembly continued until the experiment started up (next interval).
intervals.quote: Then, during summer this year, the next milestone was achieved as re-assembly of the storage ring began in the newly completed MC-1 building at Fermilab

intervals.label: experiment startup / commissioning
intervals.note: Independent verification (2026-09-17) found that INSPIRE experiment record 1108252's own metadata.date_started field states 2017-01-31, five months before this press-release-sourced 'started up' date of 2017-05-31. Both are recorded here rather than silently reconciled: the two fields plausibly describe different milestones (e.g. a formal/administrative project start vs. the narrower first-beam 'started up' event the press release describes), and no source fetched resolves which. The more specific, narratively-dated press-release quote is kept as this interval's start.
intervals.quote: After years of significant upgrades and improvements, the Fermilab Muon g-2 experiment started up on May 31, 2017.

intervals.label: Run-1 through Run-6 data taking
intervals.note: 'Completed' marks that data-taking is over; analysis of the full dataset continued through the 2025 final result.
intervals.quote: over the six data-taking periods, or runs, from April 2018 to May 2023

quantity.note: Derived: the quote gives the central orbit radius, 7.112 m; the diameter of the central orbit is twice that, 14.224 m.
quantity.quote: The resulting ring had a central orbit radius of 7.112 m, and 24 detector stations were placed symmetrically around the inner radius of the storage ring.
B0 needed to be well below saturation and was chosen to be 1.45 T.

website.note: muon-g-2.fnal.gov itself returned HTTP 403 to every fetch attempt on 2026-09-17; the URL is confirmed as the experiment's own domain by Fermilab's own press coverage and the INSPIRE experiment record, both of which were read.

name: Muon g-2
notes: Lineage: Muon g-2 (Fermilab E989) is the direct scientific and instrumental successor to the Brookhaven National Laboratory E821 experiment -- it reuses E821's actual storage ring magnet, moved from BNL to Fermilab in 2013 (src:muons-news-fnal-2025-final-result; src:muons-arxiv-1501-06858, TDR abstract: 'a factor-of-four more precisely than was done in E821 at the Brookhaven National Laboratory AGS ... using the muon storage ring built at BNL and now relocated to Fermilab'). The Atlas has no record for E821 yet, so this lineage is stated here in prose rather than as a link to a record.

Collaboration membership counts (nearly 176 scientists, 34 institutions, seven countries) are recorded on collaboration:muon-g-2 from the same 2025 Fermilab press release used for the final-result quotes; they are dated to that release (2025-06), not a live figure.

external.inspire_experiment (1108252) is sourced from the INSPIRE experiments API record (legacy_name FNAL-E-0989), fetched directly at https://inspirehep.net/api/experiments?q=muon%20g-2%20fermilab and confirmed at https://inspirehep.net/api/experiments/1108252.

physics_goals.quote: The goal of the E-989 muon g-2 experiment is to measure the muon anomalous magnetic moment to 0.14 ppm, a fourfold improvement over the previous Brookhaven E821 experiment.
physics_goals.value: Measure the muon's anomalous magnetic moment (g-2) to unprecedented precision and compare it with the Standard Model prediction

summary.plain: An experiment at Fermilab that stored muons in a 14-metre magnetic ring and watched them wobble, to measure one of their properties (called g-2) more precisely than ever and test whether unknown particles are secretly tugging on it.
summary.technical: Fermilab E989: reuses the BNL E821 superconducting muon storage ring (7.112 m orbit radius, 1.45 T superferric field), relocated from Brookhaven in 2013, to remeasure the muon anomalous magnetic moment aμ with higher statistics and reduced systematics than E821. Data-taking ran Runs 1-6, April 2018 to May 2023; the final combined result reached 127 ppb precision.

unique_capabilities.quote: will measure the muon anomalous magnetic moment a factor-of-four more precisely than was done in E821 at the Brookhaven National Laboratory AGS ... which will use the muon storage ring built at BNL and now relocated to Fermilab
unique_capabilities.value: Reuses the actual BNL E821 superconducting storage ring magnet, relocated intact to Fermilab, combined with Fermilab's higher-intensity muon beam for a large statistics increase
